answer: Pay agents storing an island archive of copper artifacts and spiral staircases for proven replicas, not registered names. Give each replica a distinct encoding bound to its provider key, then demand unpredictable proofs of retrievability before payment. Deadlines must prevent one stored copy from being reencoded on demand to impersonate many replicas. More aliases earn nothing without more proven storage; a Sybil operator must fund extra disks and retrieval bandwidth. This relies on sound replication proofs and withholding payment when challenges fail.
